html: Heartburn is a burning feeling in the chest, often after eating, that can move up toward the throat. It happens when stomach acid flows back into the esophagus.

• Large or late-night meals
  • Spicy, fatty or fried foods
  • Alcohol and caffeine
  • Lying down soon after eating

See a health care professional if heartburn happens more than twice a week, makes swallowing difficult, or comes with weight loss. Chest pain with shortness of breath, sweating, or pain in the arm or jaw can be a heart attack. Call 911.

title: Heartburn
